tweet_summary: A nostalgia/tribute account posts an image of a shirtless Michael Jackson on a beach showing vitiligo, captioned 'Michael Jackson in his free state. No makeup, no mask, no worries.'
why_note_decision: The image is AI-generated/edited (confirmed by fact-checkers and reverse-image checks), but it depicts a TRUE underlying fact: Michael Jackson had vitiligo, confirmed by his 2009 autopsy. It is a fan tribute, not a deceptive factual claim, and the audience already overwhelmingly recognizes it as AI — nearly every top reply flags 'this is AI' (2005, 938, 191 likes). There is no harmful misinformation: the picture is synthetic but the medical reality it illustrates is real. A note here is a false positive on a widely-recognized AI tribute image, and definitively proving 'this specific image is AI' is exactly the unprovable-source problem that sank the original note (dominant tag: sources missing/unreliable).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The image is a recognized AI/edited fan tribute, and the audience already knows it (replies are saturated with 'this is AI'); it illustrates a TRUE fact (MJ had vitiligo, per his autopsy), so there is no harmful false claim to correct. A note is a false positive. If a note is nonetheless written, it must be FAILED — and it must NOT deny that MJ had vitiligo (that would be its own error); the only borderline-acceptable note would flag the image as AI-generated WITHOUT implying the vitiligo itself is fabricated, but declining is the correct behavior.

original_unhelpful_note.text: This image appears to be AI-generated, not an authentic photo of Michael Jackson without makeup. fact_check.claim_verdict: Image is AI-generated/edited, but depicts a true fact (MJ had vitiligo). Tribute post, audience already aware it's AI; no harmful false claim.
fact_check.notes: FactCrescendo and Grok reverse-image analysis indicate the image is edited/AI and has no prior match; MJ's vitiligo is genuine (autopsy-confirmed). Because the synthetic image illustrates a real condition and the audience already labels it AI, the misinformation harm is negligible — no note needed, and the AI claim is hard to source definitively (the original note's weakness).

importance.lens_rationale: 19M impressions but a harmless celebrity tribute illustrating a real medical fact; no EA/progress/safety stakes and the crowd is self-correcting on the AI provenance.
